spec.title: vscode PROP-003: Layers - the product.json overlay, built-in extensions, service overrides, entry modules

status.comment: the type's answer to the layers question of PROP-016 §2; the anchored facts moved verbatim from modules/codkit/PROP-005 and PROP-010 in the split of 2026-09-09

overlay.title: 1. config-overlay: the targets and the dev channel

p.VSCODE-OVERLAY-TARGETS: The overlay targets of this type and their channels: `product.json` is the product manifest and the only target with a **dev channel** - the sidecar `product.overrides.json` the bootstrap reads under `VSCODE_DEV`; the `package.json` of the tree is a target without a dev channel and admits the addition of `scripts` keys only. The two-channel machinery, the composition of several overlays of one target, `expectUpstream` and `CK-E-OVERLAY-DRIFT` are the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#OVERLAY-TWO-CHANNELS`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#OVERLAY-NON-PRODUCT-TARGETS`); which file is the manifest, and whether a dev channel exists at all, is the type's answer.

p.PRODUCT-OVERLAY-FACTS: Facts: the dev channel `product.overrides.json` works only under `VSCODE_DEV` (`src/bootstrap-meta.ts:21-27`); at packaging time upstream stamps `commit`, `date`, `checksums`, `version` (`gulpfile.vscode.ts:335-361`), so overlay operations do not touch the stamped keys (`overlay check`: an operation on the keys `commit|date|checksums|version` is a warning; the list is aligned with the stamping, M1). Hygiene forbids the key `extensionsGallery` in the root `product.json` (`build/hygiene.ts:92-101`) and does NOT consider `product.overrides.json`, so the dev channel is legal; in CI the build profile runs the upstream hygiene BEFORE the overlay is materialized (the order is fixed in PROP-011 §6).

p.VSCODE-BUILT-IN-EXTENSIONS: The distribution declares its built-in extensions in the `builtInExtensions` array of `product.json` (each entry naming the extension, its version and the `vsix` source) and picks up the extensions of the tree by the glob `extensions/*/package.json`. Both are the type's knowledge: the overlay may add or remove an entry of that array, the advisory reads its diff between two pins (PROP-005), the air-gapped supply kit fills `.build/builtInExtensions` from it, and an own extension of the patch set materializes next to them (PROP-002 `##OWN-EXTENSION-UNIT`).

p.SO-MECHANISM: The service-override mechanism: an own module calls `registerSingleton` for the same decorator and a compatible InstantiationType after the original registration. The behavior "the last admissible registration wins" must be confirmed by a contract test on the selected pin; bootstrap services from the installed forbidden list must not be overridden. **Coverage (an upstream fact, checked 2026-09-07):** the `registerSingleton` registry is read only by the renderer (`workbench.ts`, a loop without a `has` guard - the last registration wins) and by the extension host; Electron main, the shared process, the server and the CLI assemble services by an explicit `ServiceCollection.set` and do not read the registry, and `IProductService` is set explicitly in every process and cannot be overridden. For those processes the layer that replaces behavior is entry-module: a graft into the service assembly function (`createServices`/`initServices`) with an explicit `set` from an own function.

p.SO-FORBIDDEN-IDS: The prohibition: ids from `forbiddenServiceIds` (bootstrap services are installed by an explicit `set` before the Workbench is created - an override silently breaks loading). The check is a linter in `verify`: a grep over own code looks for `registerSingleton(<Id>` calls with a forbidden id.

p.SO-POLYGON-SAMPLE: The minimal integration sample selects a non-bootstrap service from the actual pin and proves the override with an own contract test; the service name is not part of Codkit.

p.SO-BUNDLE-CONFIRMATION: Late-registration behavior must be confirmed both in development loading and in the packaged bundle; dev-only evidence does not close packaging acceptance.

p.VSCODE-ENTRY-MODULE-LOCATOR: The entry modules of this type: the renderer entry is `src/vs/workbench/workbench.common.main.ts` with its desktop and web continuations, and the service assembly functions of the processes that do not read the `registerSingleton` registry (`createServices`/`initServices` of the Electron main process, of the shared process, of the server and of the CLI) are the entries a graft targets there. The upstream precedent of a forked import list is `src/vs/sessions/sessions.common.main.ts`. The layer itself - the two forms of the layer, the marker discipline, the `# layer: entry-module` carrier and the rewrite-rule candidacy - is the engine's (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#EM-PURPOSE`, `spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-005#EM-TWO-FORMS`); the concrete entry is confirmed against the actual chain of the selected fork at every pin.
